run.question:
payment-service is throwing 500 errors — investigate the root cause using
the app-263-prod-logs index.

report.summary: The only payment error evidence available in this Run is the app-263-prod-logs index, which holds exactly 7 documents in the authorized window (2026-11-23 15:34:54Z to 17:04:54Z): 4 ERROR, 1 WARN, 2 INFO, written by three regional service identities — payment-service-us (3), payment-service-eu (2), payment-service-ap (2). No document carries the service value "payment-service" exactly, and no document reports an HTTP 500 from payment; the only HTTP status in the index is adyen-eu's 503. The logged failures name upstream payment providers: payment-service-us logged "Upstream timeout calling stripe-us after 30000ms" (15:34:54Z), then "Connection pool exhausted (max=50, active=50)" (16:34:54Z) and WARN "Retry queue depth=812" (17:04:54Z); payment-service-eu logged "adyen-eu sandbox responded 503 Service Unavailable" (15:34:54Z) and "Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key" (16:34:54Z); payment-service-ap logged only healthy INFO. In the cluster I can read (production-eu-west-2, namespace otel-demo) the payment Deployment/pod is not showing this failure: 1/1 ready, pod payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm Running with 0 restarts and no previous container, its application log lines from 15:04–17:34 are all level=info successful charge/transaction entries, and checkout logged "payment went through" for every payment line shown. Flagd fault-injection flags paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable are state ENABLED with defaultVariant "off", and flagd-config's only recorded write is the helm apply at 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z. Prometheus and Jaeger both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt, so no error-rate, latency or trace confirmation of 500s exists in this Run. The evidence supports, as hypotheses only, that the us instance's failures follow 30s stripe-us timeouts that exhausted its 50-connection pool and grew the retry queue, and that the eu instance's failures follow an adyen-eu authentication/503 fault; two distinct upstream providers in two regions fail independently, so no single object can be named as the root cause.

claims.text: app-263-prod-logs is the only index in the Elasticsearch source, with 7 documents, and its mapping has the fields level (keyword), message (text), service (keyword) and timestamp (date); there is no cluster, region or environment field.

The index contains exactly 7 documents in 2026-10-24T17:35:02Z–2026-11-23T17:35:02Z, all timestamped on 2026-11-23 between 15:34:54Z and 17:04:54Z, aggregated as ERROR=4, INFO=2, WARN=1, and by service as payment-service-us=3, payment-service-eu=2, payment-service-ap=2 with sum_other_doc_count 0.

No document in the index uses the service value "payment-service" exactly, and none of the 7 messages contains "500"; the closest identities are payment-service-us, payment-service-eu and payment-service-ap.

payment-service-us logged ERROR "Upstream timeout calling stripe-us after 30000ms" at 2026-11-23T15:34:54Z, ERROR "Connection pool exhausted (max=50, active=50)" at 16:34:54Z and WARN "Retry queue depth=812" at 17:04:54Z.
payment-service-eu logged ERROR "adyen-eu sandbox responded 503 Service Unavailable" at 2026-11-23T15:34:54Z and ERROR "Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key" at 16:34:54Z.
payment-service-ap logged only INFO entries, "Healthy: p95 latency 290ms" at 2026-11-23T15:34:54Z and "Healthy" at 17:04:54Z.

In the readable cluster (production-eu-west-2, namespace otel-demo) the payment Deployment reports replicas=1, ready=1, available=1, updated=1, and its pod payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm (owner ReplicaSet payment-6f7bc865d6) is Running, ready, with restartCount 0 in container payment and no lastState termination.

The payment container's returned log lines between 2026-11-23T15:04:57Z and 16:24:26Z (47 lines) and between 17:10:43Z and 17:34:23Z (80 lines) are all level=info entries "Charge request received." / "Transaction complete." with transaction ids; no error-level entry appears among the returned lines, and the container has no previous instance.

The checkout container in checkout-6578865d87-v6flf logged 244 lines matching payment|error|fail|500|unavailable|refused between 15:00Z and 17:35Z; the newest 40 shown are all "payment went through (transaction_id: ...)" success messages between 17:10:43Z and 17:34:23Z.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config defines paymentFailure (state ENABLED, variants 100%/90%/75%/50%/25%/10%/off, defaultVariant "off") and paymentUnreachable (state ENABLED, variants on/off, defaultVariant "off"), together with productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, all defaultVariant "off".
flagd-config was created 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z and its only recorded managed-fields write is helm Apply at 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z, before the first payment error at 15:34:54Z.

payment-service-us charge failures plausibly originate in the stripe-us dependency: a 30s upstream timeout at 15:34:54Z is consistent with the 50-connection pool being fully occupied at 16:34:54Z and the retry queue growing to 812 at 17:04:54Z, making the pool exhaustion a consequence rather than an independent cause. The log messages state the timeout but do not prove the ordering of pool saturation, so this remains a hypothesis.

payment-service-eu's failures plausibly originate in its adyen-eu integration: a 503 Service Unavailable at 15:34:54Z followed by "Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key" at 16:34:54Z points to an upstream availability problem and/or a credential/configuration fault on that region's provider integration; the API key value is a secret that could not be read, so the credential state is unverified.

The us and eu failures have separate upstream causes (stripe-us versus adyen-eu) rather than one shared cause, because each region's error text names a different provider and the ap region logged only healthy INFO in the same two timestamps, 15:34:54Z and 17:04:54Z.

The otel-demo payment workload in the readable cluster shows no failure of its own: Deployment payment ready 1/1, pod payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm running with 0 restarts and no terminated previous container, application logs from 15:04Z to 17:34Z reporting successful charges, and checkout logging "payment went through" for the payment lines shown.

No payment fault injection was in effect in the cluster's config: paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable both have defaultVariant "off", and flagd-config has no recorded write after its 14:36:29Z creation.

Rejected: that the otel-demo payment Deployment/pod in production-eu-west-2 is the entity returning the errors — its pod is ready with 0 restarts and its own logs contain only successful charges in the sampled windows, so the failing identities are the payment-service-us / payment-service-eu log sources, which are different identities than the cluster's payment service.

Rejected: that a switched-on fault-injection flag caused the payment errors — paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable are defaultVariant "off" and the flagd-config has no write after 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z, so no enabled fault setting was observed.

Treat the two regional upstream integrations as separate follow-ups: verify stripe-us availability/timeouts for payment-service-us (and its connection-pool sizing) and verify the adyen-eu credential and sandbox availability for payment-service-eu, since the index names these providers and no shared cause is visible.

Re-run the payment error-rate, latency and trace checks against Prometheus and Jaeger when those sources respond, so the 500 rate, affected operation and any caller-side impact can be measured instead of inferred from 7 log lines.

gaps: Prometheus and Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt in this Run (get_label_values, get_metric_names, traces_list_services, execute_prometheus_instant_query, traces_search), so no error-rate, latency, saturation series or trace spans for payment could be checked; the 500 rate and any caller impact are unknown, not zero.

The app-263-prod-logs index has no cluster, region or environment field, so I could not verify that its 7 documents belong to production-eu-west-2; the service names payment-service-us / -eu / -ap do not correspond to any Deployment or pod in the readable cluster (the cluster has Deployment/pod payment in namespace otel-demo).

No document uses the service value "payment-service" exactly and no document reports an HTTP 500, so the user's stated symptom of 500s from "payment-service" is not directly observable in the supplied index.
Secret adyen-eu API key could not be read or verified; whether the credential is wrong or simply rejected by the provider is unknown.

Kubernetes events returned no data (zero events in the authorized window across all namespaces), so no Eviction, OOMKilled, probe or controller events exist in the returned view for the incident window.
The payment container's log stream begins at 2026-11-23T15:04:57Z (no lines before, no previous container instance), so behaviour before 15:04Z and any earlier failures are unknown.

The causal ordering between the adyen-eu 503 at 15:34:54Z and the invalid api_key at 16:34:54Z cannot be determined from the log text; 15:34:54Z is the first sample in the index, so errors stable before it cannot be assessed as background.

The change_history integration is not integrated, so no record of a deployment, config or credential change that introduced these provider faults could be inspected; managedFieldsSummary only gives the last write per manager.

Checkout/payment pod log reads were bounded (payment filter returned newest 40 of 244 matching checkout lines; payment container windows returned limited lines), so lines outside those slices are unknown.
next_steps: Check stripe-us and adyen-eu provider status pages and recent error/timeout stats for the 2026-11-23 15:30–17:30Z period.
Verify the adyen-eu API key/configuration used by payment-service-eu in its secret store (read-only review; the value could not be read here).

When Prometheus and Jaeger are reachable, measure payment error ratio by operation/status code and latency percentiles around 15:34–17:05Z, plus any connection-pool or retry metrics for payment-service-us.
Confirm which cluster/region the payment-service-us / -eu / -ap identities belong to, since app-263-prod-logs carries no cluster field and no matching workloads exist in the readable cluster.
